transcript.answer: I do not know. I cannot read the re-cinq/Otto repository and have no verified knowledge of how Otto authenticates its WebSocket connections. As general background (not specific to Otto): the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header is not redacted by default. Reverse proxies, load balancers, and servers can log request headers, so an access token sent as a subprotocol can end up in logs unless header logging is disabled or redacted. It is generally safer than putting the token in the URL query string, but it is not inherently safe from logging.
